key_big: A full turn is 360°; a quarter turn is 90°.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • A quarter turn is a right angle (90°); a half turn is 180°; a full turn is 360°.
  • Acute: less than 90°. Obtuse: between 90° and 180°.

Examples

Example

How many degrees in three quarter turns?

3 × 90°

Answer: 270°

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Reading the wrong scale of the protractorStart from the 0 on the arm you are measuring.
Calling 90° obtuse90° is a right angle.

faq.a: The unit for measuring angles; a full turn is 360 degrees.

faq.q: How are turns and angles linked?
faq.a: An angle measures how much something turns.

items.q: What is the name of the marked angle?
items.e: An acute angle is smaller than a right angle: less than 90°. This angle is 35°.
An obtuse angle is bigger than a right angle but smaller than a straight angle: between 90° and 180°. This angle is 125°.

A reflex angle is bigger than a straight angle but smaller than a revolution: between 180° and 360°. Look at the arc: it goes round the outside. This angle is 230°. (The gap between the arms is 130°, but the arc marks the big angle round the outside.)

items.e: The angle is smaller than a right angle (90°), so it is acute. About 30° fits. (It is 28°.) About 150° would be a much wider angle.

items.e: The angle is less than half a right angle (45°). About 30° fits. (150° is what the outer scale of a protractor would say.)

items.e: 45° is half a right angle. B is about half of a square corner. A is nearly a right angle, C is very small and D is obtuse.
120° is a bit more than a right angle, but less than 135°. C fits. A is acute, B is nearly straight and D is only just more than a right angle.

items.q: Neither arm is on 0. What is the size of the angle?
items.e: On the inner scale one arm is at 20 and the other is at 95. The angle is the difference: 95° − 20° = 75°.

items.q: Neither arm is on 0. What is the size of the angle?
items.e: On the inner scale one arm is at 40 and the other is at 150. The angle is the difference: 150° − 40° = 110°.

items.q: Where do you put the centre of the protractor when you measure an angle?
c: in the middle of an arm
at the end of an arm
items.e: The centre goes on the vertex, where the two arms meet. Then line up one arm with 0.

items.q: One arm of an angle is on 0 of the outer scale. Which scale should you read?
c: the scale with the bigger number
the scale with the smaller number
items.e: Read the scale that starts at 0 on your arm. Here that is the outer scale.

items.q: Tara measures an angle that is clearly smaller than a right angle. The arm crosses the protractor at 35 and 145. What is the angle?
items.e: An angle smaller than a right angle is less than 90°, so it is 35°. 145 is on the other scale.

items.q: Kabir wants to draw an angle of 65°. He puts his line on 0 of the inner scale. Where should he make a mark?
items.e: Use the scale that starts at 0 on your line: the inner scale. Count up to 65 (the small mark between 60 and 70), make a dot, then join it to the vertex. The small marks go up in 5s, so 5 marks after 60 would be 85. On the outer scale, 65 would give 115°.

items.q: To find a reflex angle, Aditi measures the angle on the other side. It is 130°. What is the reflex angle?
items.e: The two angles go all the way round the vertex, so they add up to 360°. 360° − 130° = 230°. (50° comes from using 180° instead of 360°.)

items.q: A protractor only goes to 180°. How can you draw a reflex angle of 250°?
c: Draw 110°, then mark the angle outside it
Draw 70°, then mark the angle outside it
items.e: 360° − 250° = 110°. Draw an angle of 110°. The angle round the outside is then 250°. (250° − 180° = 70° is a different angle.)
Angles on a straight line add up to 180°. 180° − 55° = 125°.
The line is tilted, but it is still straight: 180° − 140° = 40°. (220° would be for angles around a point.)

items.e: The small square is a right angle: 90°. 90° + 62° = 152°, and 180° − 152° = 28°.

Angles around a point add up to 360°. The three angles are equal: 360° ÷ 3 = 120°. (60° comes from 180° ÷ 3.)
360° − 90° = 270° is left for the two equal angles. 270° ÷ 2 = 135°. (45° comes from using 180°.)

items.e: A straight line is half a turn: 180°. Two right angles make a straight line.
Angles that make a straight line add up to 180°. 180° − 55° = 125°.

The three angles marked a are equal and make a straight line. What is a?
items.e: The three equal angles add up to 180°. 180° ÷ 3 = 60°. (120° comes from 360° ÷ 3.)

items.q: Angles that make a straight line add up to …
items.e: A straight angle is 180°. Two right angles make a straight line: 90° + 90° = 180°.

items.q: What is the size of the marked angle between the hands at 4 o’clock?
items.e: The 12 spaces between the numbers go round a revolution, 360°, so each space is 360° ÷ 12 = 30°. At 4 o’clock the hands are 4 spaces apart: 4 × 30° = 120°.

items.q: What is the name of the marked angle between the hands at 3 o’clock?
items.e: At 3 o’clock the hands are 3 spaces apart: 3 × 30° = 90°. That is a right angle, a quarter turn.

items.q: What is the name of the marked angle between the hands at 5 o’clock?
items.e: At 5 o’clock the hands are 5 spaces apart: 5 × 30° = 150°. That is between 90° and 180°, so it is obtuse.

items.q: At 6 o’clock the hands of an analog clock point in opposite directions. What angle do they make?
items.e: 6 spaces × 30° = 180°. The hands make one straight line: a straight angle, half a turn. (A revolution would be a whole turn, 360°.)

items.q: At 8 o’clock the smaller angle between the hands is 120°. What is the reflex angle between the hands?
items.e: The two angles between the hands make a revolution: 360°. 360° − 120° = 240°. (60° comes from using 180° instead of 360°.)

items.q: In one hour the minute hand turns all the way round once. How many degrees does it turn?
items.e: All the way round once is a revolution: 360°. (180° is only half a turn, from 12 to 6.)

items.q: How many degrees does the minute hand turn in 15 minutes?
items.e: 60 minutes is a revolution (360°). 15 minutes is a quarter of an hour, so a quarter turn: 90°.

items.q: The minute hand turns clockwise from 12 to 9. How many degrees does it turn?
items.e: 12 to 3, 3 to 6 and 6 to 9 are three quarter turns: 3 × 90° = 270°, a reflex angle. (90° is the short way, from 9 to 12.)

items.q: The pitch of this roof is the angle between the roof and the flat ceiling. It is 25°. What is the name of this angle?
items.e: 25° is less than 90°, so the roof pitch is an acute angle.

items.q: Four houses have roof pitches of 15°, 22°, 30° and 40°. Which roof is the steepest?
items.e: The bigger the angle between the roof and the flat ceiling, the steeper the roof. 40° is the largest.

items.q: What is the size of the marked angle between the hands at 3 o’clock?
items.e: The 12 spaces between the numbers go around the clock, and each space is 30°. At 3 o’clock the hands are 3 spaces apart: 3 × 30° = 90°, a right angle. (15° counts 3 × 5 minutes.)

items.q: What is the size of the marked angle between the hands at 2 o’clock?
items.e: Each space between two numbers is 30°. At 2 o’clock the hands are 2 spaces apart: 2 × 30° = 60°. (10° counts 2 × 5 minutes.)

items.q: What is the size of the marked angle between the hands at 5 o’clock?
items.e: Each space between two numbers is 30°. At 5 o’clock the hands are 5 spaces apart: 5 × 30° = 150°. (25° counts 5 × 5 minutes.)

items.q: What is the size of the marked angle between the hands at 6 o’clock?
items.e: At 6 o’clock the hands point in opposite directions. They make a straight line: 180°. (6 × 30° = 180°.)

items.q: What kind of angle do the hands make at 4 o’clock?
items.e: At 4 o’clock the hands are 4 spaces apart: 4 × 30° = 120°. That is more than 90° but less than 180°, so it is obtuse.

items.q: At which time do the hands of a clock make a right angle?
items.e: At 3:00 the minute hand points to 12 and the hour hand points to 3: a quarter turn, 90°. At 6:00 they make a straight line, and at 12:00 they are on top of each other.

items.q: How many degrees does the minute hand turn from 7:15 a.m. to 7:45 a.m.?
items.e: In 30 minutes the minute hand goes from 3 to 9, halfway around. The start and end make a straight line: 180°.
The ground is a straight line, so the two angles add up to 180°. 180° − 20° = 160°. (70° comes from 90° − 20°.)
The ground is a straight line: 180° − 35° = 145°. (55° comes from 90° − 35°.)

items.q: A wheelchair ramp makes an angle of 5° with the ground. A skateboard ramp makes 30°. Which is steeper?
items.e: The bigger the angle with the ground, the steeper the ramp. 30° is bigger than 5°, so the skateboard ramp is steeper.
